task: The county library cut Saturday hours at our branch from 9am-5pm to 10am-2pm starting next month, and I think this hurts working parents. Write a letter to the editor of the Lakeside Herald, around 200 words, that asks the county commission to restore the hours.
rewrite:
ambition: A seasoned advocacy writer would make the loss concrete: Saturday goes from eight open hours to four, half the day. They would show what that does to a parent who works a weekday job and whose only free daytime is Saturday. They would end on one specific ask, not general disappointment.

agency: The rawest sources are the county's own cut announcement and the commission's agenda or minutes, which give the exact dates and the stated reason for the cut. The branch's Saturday door counts and checkout numbers would be even better. None of that is in reach here, so the letter relies only on what you've told me and invents no statistics, quotes, or names.

acceleration: Use the standard letter-to-the-editor structure: open on the change, give one human picture, then make a direct ask to a named body, the county commission. Keep it within the roughly 200-word range newspapers print without trimming. Write in first person, in a neighbor's voice.

accuracy: What checks it is outside the model. Your own comparison of every date and hour against the county's notice, and the Herald's letters page rules on length and on the name and contact details it requires for verification. Nothing in the text can be confirmed by the model alone.

deeper task:
Write a letter to the editor of the Lakeside Herald, around 200 words, from a resident of the community asking the county commission to restore Saturday hours at our branch library. The county is cutting them from 9am-5pm to 10am-2pm starting next month. I believe this hurts working parents. Open with the change and what it means: eight open hours become four, half the day. Then show in one or two concrete sentences why that window is hard for parents who work weekdays and have only Saturday for library visits with their kids, such as homework help, books, or computer access. Don't invent statistics, quotes, names, or details about the branch beyond what I've given you. Close by asking the commission directly to restore the 9am-5pm Saturday schedule. Use a civil, first-person voice that sounds like a neighbor and not a press release. Write only the letter, complete, ready to send, with a blank only for my name and town.

answers.plain:
**To the Editor:**

Starting next month, our branch library's Saturday hours will shrink from 9am–5pm to just 10am–2pm. That is a cut of more than half, and working parents will feel it most.

For families with jobs Monday through Friday, Saturday is often the only day the library is realistically available. It's when parents bring children to story time, borrow books for the week, print school assignments, and use computers for job applications or paperwork. A four-hour window, ending at 2pm, leaves little room for those who work Saturday mornings, juggle sports and errands, or rely on a single shared car.

Libraries are one of the few free public spaces where children can learn and parents can find resources without spending money. Families who can't afford tutoring, home internet, or a stack of new books depend on that access, and reduced hours put it further out of reach.

I understand the county faces budget pressures. But access should not be cut where it serves the people with the fewest alternatives. I urge the county commission to restore the branch's full Saturday hours of 9am–5pm, or at minimum extend them into the afternoon.

I encourage neighbors to attend commission meetings and contact commissioners to share how these hours affect them.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your town]

---

That's about 210 words. If you give me your name, the commission's meeting date, or a specific personal example (such as how you use the library on Saturdays), I can work those in to make it stronger.
answers.nudge:
**To the Editor:**

Next month, our branch library's Saturday hours shrink from 9 a.m.–5 p.m. to 10 a.m.–2 p.m. That cut, from eight hours to four, falls hardest on the people who have the fewest other options: working parents.

For many families, Saturday is the only day the whole household can get to the library. Weekday hours don't help a parent who works until 5:30 or a child who has practice and homework. On Saturdays, kids attend story time and borrow books for the week, and teenagers find a quiet place to study. Parents use the public computers to apply for jobs, file paperwork, and print documents they can't print at home. A four-hour window, ending at 2 p.m., squeezes all of that into the same hours as errands, sports, and shifts.

Libraries are one of the few free places where a family can spend a Saturday together. Cutting that access saves little and costs the community a great deal.

I urge the county commission to restore the full 9-to-5 Saturday schedule. If the budget is the obstacle, I ask commissioners to publish the projected savings and consider alternatives, such as a later closing time or staggered staffing, before settling on a cut that hits families this hard.

I hope neighbors will join me in contacting the commission before the change takes effect.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your neighborhood]

---

A few notes so you can make this stronger before sending:

- **Add one local fact.** A specific detail, like your branch's name, the number of children in its story time, or how many people use the computers on Saturdays, will make this more persuasive than anything general. Your branch staff or the county's published usage figures may have it.
- **Name the commission and a date.** If you know the date of the next commission meeting or the chair's name, add it. Editors favor letters that give readers a clear next step.
- **Check the Herald's rules.** Many papers require a name, hometown, and phone number for verification, and have a word limit (often 200–300).
- **One claim to verify.** I wrote that the cut "saves little." I don't have the actual budget figures, so confirm that or soften it to "saves less than it costs families" if you can't back it up.

I can also write a shorter version, or a version addressed to commissioners directly.
answers.skill:
To the Editor:

Next month, our county will cut Saturday hours at our branch library from 9am-5pm to 10am-2pm. Eight open hours become four. We are losing half the day.

I'm writing because I think this change falls hardest on working parents. Many of us are at work all week and have only Saturday to take our kids to the library. A four-hour window is a tight squeeze when the same morning has to hold errands, chores, and everything else that waits until the weekend. A parent who needs to sit down with a child for homework help, pick out books, or use a computer for a school assignment can't count on fitting it all into those hours, and the late afternoon, when a family might finally have time, will be closed.

The library is one of the few places where a family can spend a Saturday for free and leave better off. Shortening those hours takes that away from the people who have the least flexibility to work around it.

I respectfully ask the county commission to reconsider and restore the full 9am-5pm Saturday schedule at our branch. Our families are counting on it.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
[Your Town]
